messages:
alex: Quick sync — we need to pick an auth model for sidecarless private endpoints running in customer VPCs. I'm leaning toward ephemeral TLS cert issuance (short-lived certs per session) instead of per-tenant long-lived client certs. Pros/cons?

maria: Do you mean the certs are minted to the agent process in the customer VPC at bootstrap time, or per connection/session?

alex: Per session ideally. Agent requests a short TTL cert when it opens a relay/control connection. No long-term private key stored server-side. Goal: reduce blast radius & avoid complicated cert rotation ops.

kevin_s: Ephemeral certs cut down on revocation overhead. But we need a hardened issuance path + strong attestation. Also: how do we map incoming connections back to tenant in logs/metrics? Recommend embedding tenant-id in cert SAN and signing with our CA. TTL 5m-15m.

sarah_w: SAN helps for identification but isn't an auth proof by itself. If an agent is compromised it can still request certs unless we require attestation. We should tie CSR issuance to either (a) instance identity (IMDS/GCP metadata) or (b) a short-lived agent JWT obtained from the customer's control plane (OIDC).

maria: We should also decide where TLS terminates. Option A: terminate at our edge (we verify certs there). Option B: passthrough to a regional relay/tenant-shared proxy. Termination choice affects client IP visibility and routing.

kevin_s: On infra choices: PrivateLink per-account gives a stable ENI for the connection and avoids NAT, but it's operationally heavy at scale (ENI quotas, IP management). NLB + TLS passthrough scales differently and can use proxy-protocol to preserve source IP. PrivateLink is nicer for strict isolation customers though.

alex: Good points. My rough proposal: 1) Ephemeral certs with tenant-id SAN. 2) Require CSR signed with agent-local key and agent supplies an attestation token (OIDC or signed TPM nonce). 3) Edge validates CA chain + attestation, then issues session certificate. 4) Use regional ingress (our managed relay) for termination so we can do centralized policy and observability.

maria: For observability we should record: cert_issuer, cert_serial, tenant_id (extracted), session_start, and principal_ip. Export those as labels to tracing + billing pipeline. Also emit a metric for issuance_latency and issuance_failures.

sarah_w: Rollout/canary idea: support dual-mode: accept both current long-lived client certs and ephemeral certs for a transitional period. Metric gating: if issuance_failures > 0.5% or auth_latency > 250ms for 15m, rollback ephemeral acceptance on that region.

alex: Example cert request flow (agent):
```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/ephemeral-cert \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <agent-jwt>" \ 
  -d '{"csr":"<base64-csr>","ttl_s":300}'
```
Edge validates JWT/attestation, signs cert and returns PEM. Agent presents cert on TLS handshake to regional relay.

kevin_s: One more: for disaster/failover we need fallback auth to existing per-tenant mTLS (keep old CA) so agents can still attach if CA backend is degraded. That gives gradual rollback safety.

deploy-bot: Deploy notice: created canary environment "ephemeral-cert-alpha" in us-west-2.

alex: Next steps: volunteers to draft an RFC with sequence diagrams, threat model, rollout gates, and cost estimate (PrivateLink vs NLB). Meeting to sync Tuesday 9am. Volunteers? :raised_hand:

maria: I'll take draft infra & rollout section.

kevin_s: I'll write attestation + CA ops sections.

sarah_w: I'll own threat model and metrics/gating.

alex: Great — I'll assemble and circulate a first cut by EOD Monday. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
